ICE special agents and officers from our Portland offices arrested CONVICTED RAPIST Cristobal Felipe-Sarmiento, of Mexico, during a targeted operation in Salem, Oregon, April 9.   

A Marion County jury convicted him of first-degree rape and first-degree sodomy in Salem Dec. 19, 2016. Local reports indicate that he was initially charged with one count of first-degree rape, one count of strangulation and two counts of first-degree sodomy. 

He was handed an eight-year prison sentence and released back into the community upon his release, despite having no right to be in the country.

ALLIANCE PROTECTS CONSUMERS BY TARGETING FAKE DRUGS & CRIMINALS PROFITING FROM THEM

The ICE HSI-led @IPRCenter and the International Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Consortium (Rx-360) announced a new partnership April 6 to enhance supply chain security and prevent unauthorized products from infiltrating legitimate markets.

The alliance combines the IPR Center’s investigative expertise at disrupting criminal organizations involved in counterfeit pharmaceuticals and medical devices with Rx-360’s global network of pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers.

tweets.text:
ICE asked Long Island law enforcement to detain a Venezuelan national charged with attempted murder after allegedly trying to slash his billiards partner’s throat at Gilgo Beach February 28.

The Suffolk County DA alleged Ruben Guanipa Ramirez picked up the victim from his home, went to a pool hall, and eventually brought him to one of the most iconic murder sites in the state.

At Gilgo Beach, Guanipa Ramirez allegedly came up behind the victim, covered his mouth with a cloth, stabbed him and tried to slit his throat.

Ramirez was arrested later that same day in Nassau County. Investigators say his vehicle contained three kitchen knives, one which appeared covered in blood, rope, duct tape, blankets, plastic drop cloths, a large-wheeled bag, gloves and a boxcutter.

The suspect entered the U.S. in June 2019 on a B-2 tourist visa which required him to depart the U.S. by December 2019. Now, he faces attempted murder and assault charges in connection with the alleged incident.

Regardless of the result of the criminal case, he is not authorized to be in the United States.
